patterns.statement: Moving a rook, such as Rf1-e1, does not prove that a pawn break such as f4 is no longer a future plan.

applicability.description: Only when the question treats a rook relocation as deciding a pawn-break plan in a closed-center position. It is not attached to every board that has a rook.

patterns.statement: Ndf3 can have both attacking and defensive geometry. Occupying f3 blocks the f-pawn and does not by itself prove the knight's only function.

applicability.description: Only when the question is about Ndf3 or a d2 knight going to f3, and that move is legal from d2 on this exact FEN.

patterns.statement: A knight that attacks or supports a pawn does not, by itself, prove that the strategy is restraint.

applicability.description: Only when the question claims a knight attack proves a restraint strategy. It is not applied merely because a knight and a pawn are both on the board.
